description.detail: Pruning is a post-processing chain of workflow steps, not a filter in the relation declarations. Every relation emits candidates with the evidence a decision needs (source score and sources, target count, measured activity). The annotation fields (verdict, annotation_rule, annotation_confidence, annotation_reason) are declared properties of every node and edge, inherited from two abstract categories, and every binding seeds them with keep and three empty arrays. publish_annotated_records re-publishes each component's records unchanged under the annotated opening. annotate_rule_matches contributes one step per rule and component it governs; each step appends that rule's mark (module, confidence, reason) where its predicate holds and sets the verdict to prune. project_kept_records keeps the records whose verdict is keep and keeps the schema intact; write_facts_graph writes graph.jsonl without the four declared fields, so the shipped file carries facts and no editorial field. Two writers publish the two outputs, and reconcile_outputs fails the build unless annotated minus pruned equals shipped for nodes and edges. A rule is one module with its own predicate, confidence, reason and boundary tests; adding a rule adds a step and changes no other step.
description.numbers: annotated 74,747 nodes / 239,939 edges; shipped 28,359 / 150,856; four annotation fields absent from the shipped file

subject: B-32
title: Pruning is a post-processing projection: one annotated graph, two outputs
